## Changes to immigration instructions

We update immigration instructions regularly to reflect changes in government policy. The Minister of Immigration certifies all changes.

We include changes to instructions in the Amendment Circulars. These describe changes to the Operational Manual the Minister of Immigration has certified.

More information about our decision-making is available in:

  * Internal Administration Circulars, which describe changes to the procedures and processes that INZ staff follow
  * Advice to staff, which contain information about how to interpret instructions in the Operational Manual, and how to make correct and fair decisions.

### Receiving updates

You can sign up to receive Amendment Circulars by email.

Sign up for Amendment Circular updates

# About this manual

The Immigration New Zealand (INZ) Operational Manual contains the immigration instructions that people who want to come to New Zealand permanently or for a short time must follow. It includes the criteria that applicants must meet, the evidence they must produce to show that they meet the criteria, and the processes INZ follow to assess and verify applications. The Manual also contains information about INZ's work in protecting New Zealand's border and determining claims for refugee status. By publishing the Operational Manual, INZ meets its requirements under section 25 of the Immigration Act 2009 to publish Government instructions on granting visas. This Manual is not:

  * a step-by-step guide to work processes; or
  * a replacement for the legislation that governs INZ operations.

# Keeping up to date with immigration policy

Immigration New Zealand regularly updates immigration policy. We publish changes online, in the operational manual, and keep immigration advisers and the public up to date.

## Operational Manual

The rules and processes people must follow before we can give them a visa or permission to enter New Zealand are called 'immigration instructions'. They include requirements an applicant must meet, and evidence they must provide.

These instructions are published in our Operational Manual, which is available online.

We regularly update the Operational Manual to reflect any changes made to government policy and the immigration instructions.

The online manual includes advice on how to use it.

Operational Manual online

Other Operational Manual documents

## Amendment circulars

Upcoming changes to immigration instructions are published in amendment circulars and incorporated into the Operational Manual on the day they come into force.

Policy Amendment Circulars

## Internal administration circulars

Internal administration circulars (IACs) explain internal processes and procedures to immigration staff. We publish IACs when we need to clarify instructions in the Operational Manual.

Internal Administration Circulars (IACs)

## Advice to immigration staff

‘Advice to immigration staff’, or Visa Paks, are regular advice given to staff about how to interpret and apply immigration instructions.

We update advice to reflect best practice as immigration instructions change.

How often it publishes

Amended by amendment circular, several times a year; the index page prints 'Manual updated on:' with a date (7 October 2026 when read on 11 October 2026).

2026-10-11 · due again 2026-12-10

And sooner when

the 'Manual updated on' date on https://www.immigration.govt.nz/opsmanual/35439.htm changes · an amendment circular is issued · the 'Effective' date on a cited instruction page changes, or the instruction appears under PREVIOUS IMMIGRATION INSTRUCTIONS · a change of government or of the Immigration Minister

## Finding a document here

The manual is one document in nine parts, not a library of separate instruments, and every provision carries a code - `R2.1`, `W2.2.1`, `S4.5` - which is how it is cited and the fastest way to reach it. The contents tree on the left opens part by part; the search box matches whole words unless Match partial words is ticked. An address carries a fragment like `#35439.htm`, and those numbers are the publishing system's, not the instruction's, so they move when the manual is rebuilt.

## What it carries

  * Administration How applications are received, assessed and decided.
  * Residence The instructions for staying permanently.
  * Temporary entry class visa Visitor, work and student instructions.
  * Transit visa
  * Border Entry What happens on arrival, and who is turned away.
  * Compliance Deportation, liability and enforcement.
  * Refugees and protection
  * Appendices Skill lists, occupation tables and the schedules the instructions point at.

Served in English. As html. The newest item listed on 2026-10-28 was the manual as updated on 20 October 2026.

## What is not published here

It states the instructions, not the law. Where it summarises the Immigration Act 2009 or the Immigration Regulations 2010, it says of itself that those summaries are declaratory only and that the legislation prevails wherever the two are read differently - and that the summarised provisions are not themselves Government immigration instructions. So a requirement can be cited from here; the statutory provision behind it has to be read in the Act.
